newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FERGUSON EXPLAINS HIS RELATIONSHIP WITH CANTONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERGUSON EXPLAINS HIS RELATIONSHIP WITH CANTONA.

text.p: Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson has revealed the extent of his relationship with Eric Cantona by declaring: "Eric knows he can depend on me."
Ferguson discloses in an interview with a soccer magazine published on Wednesday that he never criticises the Frenchman in public and keeps any criticism private.

"He knows I don't desert my players," says the United boss, who feels his loyalty to the player - even after the notorious incident when he kicked a Crystal Palace fan - has been the crucial factor behind the club's remarkable success in recent years.
"Players get it between the eyeballs generally if it's criticism, but Eric knows that whatever happens, it will be in my dressing room or in my office and that's the end of it.
"I don't bear grudges, I don't have the time, and it's not part of my management strategy."

Ferguson, whose club won the league and Cup double last season, recalls that the 1.2 million pounds ($1.88 million) signing of Cantona was seen as a reckless gamble with some predicting it would cost him his job.
But the United boss says he never had any doubts about signing him, despite people pointing out the Frenchman's deficiencies.
"People went on and on about Eric couldn't do this or that. That's the problem with the game nowadays. Everybody worries about what someone can't do."

In the same interview Ferguson claims he would have retained striker Andy Cole even if he, rather than Newcastle boss Kevin Keegan, had been able to secure the signature of Alan Shearer from Blackburn this summer.
"I thought Cole played well in a lot of games, but 13 goals was ridiculous for a player of his talent," he says.
"He is capable of scoring 30 goals this season. And that was why even if we'd got Shearer, there was no way we were going to let Cole go."
Cole missed several games through injury this season and is now seen as a back-up for emerging Norwegian striker Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.
